summary_points: Document title: Ultrasonic Examination Procedure
Client: Arizona Solar One
Project: HEX replacement TES Solana
Prepared by Joanna Teixeira, reviewed and approved by Jon Baranda from LOINTEK
Procedure for ultrasonic inspections of full penetration welds in materials thicker than 8mm
Equipment requirements include pulse-echo ultrasonic equipment with specific frequency range and sensitivity control
Calibration blocks are used for distance and sensitivity calibration, with specific material and heat treatment requirements
Surface preparation involves removing weld spatter and foreign material from the base material
Welds must be prepared if surface finishing does not allow correct examination.
Temperature differential between calibration block and examination surfaces should be within 25ºF (14ºC).
Ultrasonic equipment needs to be calibrated annually or before first use.
Calibration involves checking screen height linearity and amplitude control linearity.
Straight beam calibration requires adjusting time base using specific blocks.
Angle beam calibration also uses the basic calibration block for sensitivity (DAC) calibration.
Frequency of calibration includes at the beginning, during changes in variables, and after operator change.
Examination guidelines include speed limits, overlap requirements, and reference level adjustments.
Straight beam examination is mandatory to detect potential reflectors affecting angle beam results.
The angle of the transducer is determined by examination direction and weld geometry.
Parallel exploration to the weld uses an angle beam parallel to the weld axis.
Perpendicular exploration uses an angle beam at right angles to the weld axis.
Discontinuities exceeding 20% of the reference level require investigation.
Unacceptable discontinuities include cracks, lack of fusion, and incomplete breakthroughs.
Final reports must document job number, drawings, equipment, and more.
Calibration blocks are used for calibration purposes.
